messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected in production (us-west-2). Metric: decode_tail_latency.p99 > 1500ms for 3m. Streaming stalls increased. Linked dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/2240001234
alex: ack. I'm on it. tagging @maya and @samir for kernel/compile path changes.
maya: watching. any recent TRT/FlashAttention or compiler flag rollouts in the last 30m?
samir: yep — there was a rolling flag flip 18m ago: enable_flashattn_kernel=true on runtime-kernel v2.3.4. commit: 9f3b2c. CI job: deploy-runtime-9876. (I bumped a perf flag to try reduce mem).
devops-bot: deploy-runtime-9876 -> success on 6/8 canaries, roll to 50% at 18:03 UTC.
alex: ok. can we check p95/p99 per-pool and whether streaming stalls map to kernel hosts?
jun: querying traces.. giving summary:
```
- pool: pool-alpha (older kernel) p99=260ms p95=130ms
- pool: pool-beta (new kernel) p99=1780ms p95=420ms
- error ratio increased for streaming connections on pool-beta
```
jun: stack traces show long waits in kv-cache::read() and at attention_kernel::forward() path.
lia: customer-impact quick check: top noisy tenants hitting pool-beta: [Redwood-Corp, AtlasAI, Formally]. No large 5xx, primarily timeouts/stream stalls. CS pinged.
maya: looks like the new FlashAttention kernel path is regressing tail for long-context streaming. probable interaction with our compile flags. revert plan: 1) pin traffic away from pool-beta -> pool-alpha 2) rollback enable_flashattn_kernel flag on remaining nodes 3) start canary rollback and observe.
samir: prepared rollback command:
```
# rollback flag on node pool-beta (canary)
kubectl annotate node pool-beta-canary redwood/runtime-flag-rollback=enable_flashattn_kernel:revert
kubectl rollout restart ds/runtime-kernel -n prod --field-selector spec.nodeName=pool-beta-canary
```
alex: doing step 1: rerouting 30% -> pool-alpha now. will monitor.
(devops-bot): Traffic routing updated: pool-alpha +30% applied.
~2m later~
alex: p95 dropped from 420ms -> 180ms on affected routes; p99 down from 1780ms -> 320ms. streaming stalls rate down ~85%.
lia: notifying CS: "We observed a transient latency spike tied to a recent kernel flag rollout affecting us-west-2. We've rerouted traffic and are rolling back the flag; will follow up with RCA."
samir: rolling flag on the remaining pool-beta hosts now. command: `kubectl patch daemonset/runtime-kernel -p '{"spec": {...}}'` (ops).
maya: also adding temporary fallback policy: if decode tail > 700ms then route to compatibility-model-1 (lower perf but stable).
oncall-next: I'm taking handoff in 30m. current state: rollback in progress, p99 normalized on canary and partial rollouts, routing rules active. checklist for handoff:
- verify rollback complete on all pool-beta hosts
- monitor p95/p99 for 15m post-rollback
- keep CS ticket updated and collect HV logs for affected tenants
- schedule kernel-flag revert and deeper root-cause with eng-runtime

alex: notes for follow-up/repro: reproduce with long streaming context (~4096 tokens) + KV cache enabled + batch size > 1. Samir set up repro job: `stress-decode --model gptx --seq 4096 --kv-true --batch 2`.
samir: pushed trace capture collector to /tmp/traces/2240001234, saved kernel timing histograms.
maya: tentative root cause hypothesis: flashattn kernel optimization path increases shuffle/atomic usage under long context which worsens contention with our kv-cache access pattern. compiler flag ordering changed register allocation. Needs perf debug with flame graphs.
lia: CS update posted. customers flagged: Redwood-Corp support id 8742, AtlasAI support id 8821. no escalations yet.
alex: will keep this thread updated. leaving a note for oncall-next: if latency resurges, immediate mitigation = enable fallback routing rule + open incident.
oncall-next: ack. I'll be primary on-call for next 4 hours. leaving reaction :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: severity=high -> monitoring for 2h.
alex: closing active triage for now; creating post-incident ticket: ENG-3221 (kernel/flashattn-tail-regression). assign: @maya, @samir.
